unit.why: A single narrative: R. Ozer, childless, travels to R. Zvi with a note from his father-in-law R. Feivush; R. Zvi finds the note, promises a son, and serves as sandak; the two tzaddikim then dispute who should lead the grace after meals.

stories.start_quote: הרב ר' עוזר חתנו של הרה״ק ר׳ פייבוש
stories.end_quote: קומט זיך טאקע אייך דעס בענטשין
stories.summary_en: The childless R. Ozer hides a seemingly disrespectful note from his father-in-law R. Feivush of Bolshovtsy; R. Zvi finds it in his pocket and explains that it holds name-combinations from the Priestly Blessing. He promises a son on condition he is sandak, and at the circumcision meal the two tzaddikim playfully dispute who should lead the zimmun.
